criterion: One saturated colour appears across the whole index, and every other element on the page wears a neutral.
evaluation_rule: A SATURATED COLOUR is a hue a reader would name as a colour rather than as a grey. Yes when a single saturated hue appears anywhere on the index. No when a second saturated hue turns up on any band.

criterion: Prose on the index sits in one family and every band label, date, run-log value and diagram annotation sits in a monospaced family.
evaluation_rule: A MONOSPACED FAMILY is one whose characters all occupy the same width. Yes when the paragraphs are proportional and the instrument text is monospaced throughout. No when a run-log value or a diagram annotation shares the family of the paragraphs.

criterion: The marker travelling down the left rail of the index wears the accent colour.
evaluation_rule: THE MARKER is the small solid triangle showing how far down the document a reader has come. Yes when that triangle is the saturated hue. No when the triangle is grey, or wears a hue other than the one the page uses as its accent.

criterion: Every control on the studio and the desk shows a resting, a pointed-at, a pressed, a focused and an unavailable appearance.
evaluation_rule: AN UNAVAILABLE CONTROL is one a reader can see but cannot act on. Yes when each control changes appearance under the pointer, under press, under focus and when unavailable. No when a control looks the same under the pointer as at rest.

criterion: The nine bands of the index are separated by space alone, with any rule between chapters drawn as a single hairline in pale sand.
evaluation_rule: A BAND is one of the nine chapters of the index. Yes when the gap between two bands is enough to read them as separate chapters. No when every boundary carries a heavy divider, or two bands run together with too little space between them.

criterion: Figures in a run log line up along one right edge so the four values read down a single column.
evaluation_rule: A RUN LOG is the four-row block beneath a system diagram. Yes when the four values share one right edge. No when the values sit ragged or flush against their labels.

criterion: The index runs on an even grey ramp from a near-white ground to a near-black text tone.
evaluation_rule: AN EVEN GREY RAMP is a set of neutral tones whose steps look equally far apart to the eye. Yes when the index moves through several grey steps that each read as a distinct tone. No when two of the greys are so close together that a reader reads them as one tone.

criterion: Body paragraphs in the experience band hold their lines to around sixty characters however wide the window is opened.
evaluation_rule: A MEASURE is the number of characters on one line of a paragraph. Yes when a paragraph stops growing once the window is wide, holding near sixty characters a line. No when a paragraph runs the full width of a wide window.

criterion: Movement across the index shares one easing that arrives fast and settles late, on the headline entrance, on hover and on a scrubbed diagram alike.
evaluation_rule: AN EASING is the shape a movement takes over time. Yes when every animated moment on the index starts quickly and slows into place. No when one moment eases differently from the rest, such as a linear hover beside an eased entrance.

criterion: A gate mark inside a system diagram collapses to a sliver of its height and dims as the diagram is scrolled through, holding that state afterwards.
evaluation_rule: A GATE MARK is the drawn element standing for a gate in the diagram. Yes when the mark shrinks in height and dims at one point in the scroll and stays that way. No when the gate mark holds one appearance through the whole scroll, or springs back to its full height.

criterion: The principle numbers in the philosophy band wear a deep blue and carry their meaning through position and size too.
evaluation_rule: A SECOND SIGNAL is anything besides hue that tells a reader what an element means. Yes when a reader seeing the philosophy band in grey alone can still tell which principle is which. No when hue is the only thing separating the numbers from the surrounding text.

criterion: The rail marker, the scroll cue, the chapter rule and the theme control each take their colour from the text around them.
evaluation_rule: TAKING COLOUR FROM THE TEXT AROUND THEM means a glyph changes tone when the text beside it does. Yes when all four glyphs follow their surrounding text colour under a high-contrast rendering. No when one of them holds a fixed tone the surrounding text has left behind.

criterion: At phone width every diagram on the index takes a taller arrangement, running its stages down the screen at a readable size.
evaluation_rule: A TALLER ARRANGEMENT stacks the stages of a diagram down the screen. Yes when a diagram at phone width runs its stages down a column at a size a reader can follow. No when the same wide drawing is squeezed sideways into the phone width.

criterion: At phone width the left rail of the index is gone and the contact control has become a bar across the foot of the screen.
evaluation_rule: A BAR ACROSS THE FOOT spans the full width at the bottom of the window. Yes when the rail is absent at phone width and the contact control spans the foot. No when the rail is still shown, or the contact control keeps floating against the right edge.
